title: Banh Mi
subtitle: Vietnamese baguette sandwich with pickled vegetables and pate
excerpt: A brilliant collision of French colonial baking and Vietnamese flavours. The key is contrast: crisp baguette, rich filling, sharp pickled carrot and daikon, fresh coriander and a hit of chilli.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from classic Vietnamese banh mi preparations documented in multiple culinary sources.

recipe.batchNotes: The pickled vegetables keep for up to 2 weeks in the fridge. The pork filling keeps for 3 days refrigerated. Assemble sandwiches fresh.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the pickles at least 1 hour (ideally overnight) before serving. The pork filling can be made a day ahead.

content.text: Banh mi is assembled rather than cooked: the real work is in the components. The baguette should be Vietnamese-style if you can find it (lighter and crispier than French), but any good baguette from a bakery works. Buy four individual baguettes or cut a long one into quarters. The filling here is a classic caramelised pork, but the pickles and herbs are what make the sandwich sing.

items.prepNote: peeled and cut into thin matchsticks

content.text: Make the pickles first. Combine the rice vinegar, caster sugar and half a teaspoon of fine salt in a bowl. Stir until the sugar dissolves. Add the carrot matchsticks, toss well and press down so they are submerged. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. The longer they sit, the more they mellow and pickle.

Mix the pork filling. Combine the pork mince, soy sauce, fish sauce, garlic, ginger, palm sugar and sesame oil in a bowl. Mix well with your hands or a fork. Leave to marinate for 15 minutes while you prepare the other components.

Cook the pork. Heat the sunflower oil in a large frying pan over high heat until shimmering. Add the pork mixture in a single layer as much as possible. Leave it untouched for 2 minutes to develop a deep caramelised crust underneath, then break it up and stir-fry for another 3 to 4 minutes until cooked through and sticky. The sugar in the marinade should caramelise and colour the meat.
Warm the baguettes. Place them in a hot oven at 200 C for 5 minutes to crisp the crust. This step matters: a soft baguette will collapse when filled.

Assemble the sandwiches. Split each baguette lengthways but not all the way through. Spread mayonnaise along both cut sides. Lay in the cucumber strips, then add the hot pork filling. Drain the pickled carrots well and pile them on top. Add spring onion, coriander and chilli slices. Close and eat immediately.

items.symptom: Pork filling is pale and stewed rather than caramelised and sticky
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough, or the filling was stirred too soon.
items.fix: Get the pan very hot before adding the pork. Do not stir for the first 2 minutes. If needed, increase the heat and cook off any liquid before the caramelisation can happen.

items.symptom: Pickled carrots are too sharp and acidic
items.cause: Not enough sugar in the pickling liquid, or too little pickling time for the flavours to mellow.
items.fix: Add a pinch more sugar to the pickling liquid and stir. Allow the carrots to pickle for longer: overnight gives a much more balanced flavour than 1 hour.

items.cause: The filling was too wet, or the bread was not crisped before filling.
items.fix: Always crisp the baguette in a hot oven first. Drain the pickled carrots thoroughly. Assemble and eat within a few minutes of filling.
